paper_metadata.title: Optimized Quantum Circuit Implementation of Payoff Function

summary: This paper presents optimized gate-based quantum circuits for the call option payoff function f_K(S)=max(S-K,0), with two main variants: a space-efficient version with Toffoli-depth n and a time-efficient version with Toffoli-depth 1. It compares multiple adders and Toffoli decompositions analytically; for example, the Cuccaro f1 circuit with Zero decomposition uses 3n+1 qubits, 21n T gates, and 9n T-depth, while the f2 variant with Four decomposition reaches 2n+1 T-depth, but no classical baseline or hardware execution is reported.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum circuit implementations of the call option payoff function f_K(S)=max(S-K,0), including space-efficient and time-efficient variants, with resource comparisons across multiple quantum adders and Toffoli decompositions.

algorithm.variant: optimized quantum circuit for call option payoff function; space-efficient and time-efficient implementations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: n-bit registers for S and K; subtraction performed via two's complement using bitwise X gates and quantum adders; result stored in an additional register to ensure reversibility
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: reversibility handled by storing the result in an output register and using a sign qubit to conditionally zero the output when S-K is negative

problem_instance.description: Call option payoff computation for n-bit values of underlying asset price S and strike price K

dataset_specification.description: n-bit arithmetic instances; no market dataset used

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical resource estimation and comparison across circuit constructions; no empirical runtime or shot-based evaluation reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Two's complement subtraction; bitwise inversion of K or S using X gates; adder selection among Cuccaro, Draper, Takahashi, Gidney, Higher Radix

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical pricing baseline or empirical speedup is reported; the paper is a quantum circuit resource-estimation study.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper reports analytical resource trade-offs for payoff circuits: f1 has Toffoli-depth n and f2 has Toffoli-depth 1, with qubit counts and T-depth formulas varying by adder and Toffoli decomposition (e.g., Cuccaro f1 Zero: 3n+1 qubits, 21n T gates, 9n T-depth; f2 Four: 4n+4 qubits, 2n+1 T-depth).
limiting_factors: No empirical quantum-vs-classical benchmark is reported
No hardware execution or noise study is provided
No classical pricing baseline is compared
Results are symbolic/asymptotic resource estimates only

notes: No specific hardware or framework is reported; the paper is a circuit/resource-estimation study only.
num_qubits and circuit depth are reported as formulas/tables dependent on n and adder/Toffoli-decomposition choice, not as a single fixed value.
No asymptotic quantum advantage over classical algorithms is claimed; the paper focuses on resource trade-offs.
